title: Body Harvest
subtitle: DMA Design · Nintendo 64
summary: Body Harvest is DMA Design's Nintendo 64 action adventure about Adam Drake, a soldier travelling through time to stop aliens from harvesting Earth's population. body: Body Harvest is DMA Design's Nintendo 64 action adventure about Adam Drake, a soldier travelling through time to stop aliens from harvesting Earth's population. The campaign moves between periods and regions, including Greece, Java and the United States, with people to protect and a threat developing across each area. Adam explores on foot and commandeers vehicles, giving the player several ways to approach the surrounding terrain. The next useful machine can change both the speed of travel and the means available for confronting an attacking creature.

Cars, boats and aircraft extend the expedition beyond the soldier's own movement. Entering one changes which route can be taken and how an encounter can be handled, while leaving it returns attention to local exploration and the people nearby. The player has to respond to the invasion as it develops rather than only move toward a fixed exit. A distant attack can make another destination urgent, connecting navigation through the region to the survival of its inhabitants.

Originally planned around the Nintendo 64's launch, the project underwent substantial changes and eventually reached release in 1998 through different publishers. DMA Design was also developing Grand Theft Auto during this period. Body Harvest's interest in moving between a person and accessible vehicles gave its large regions a distinctive structure. The result can be demanding and uneven, but its central ambition is clear: a landscape should contain several practical ways to travel and act, with the player choosing which one the current emergency needs.
